behavioral_effects: A scheduled access-token refresh no longer tears down the chat WebSocket while a turn is streaming or waiting on approval; the rotated token is applied lazily after the turn settles (immediately when idle or when the socket already dropped).

stop, resume, and ask_user_response frames arriving on a socket with no in-flight turn are answered with turn_not_active instead of being dropped silently; the frontend reconciles by erroring orphaned tool blocks, closing the streaming message with a visible note, and re-enabling input. The same reconcile runs when a fresh socket opens while local state still claims a turn is in flight.
Logout still tears the socket down (the applied connect token is cleared when the in-memory token goes null).
compatibility_impact: Additive WebSocket event turn_not_active (producer backend/app/services/agent_session.py, consumer frontend/src/hooks/use-chat.ts) - both sides ship together, so the websocket-events-have-producers-and-consumers contract is satisfied; older frontends ignore unknown event types. No REST, schema, or migration changes.
follow_up: Backend turn survival across reconnect (resume a live turn on a new socket) remains the larger fix if long turns must survive genuine network drops, not just scheduled refreshes.
limitations: The generated WebSocket event inventory (interfaces.json websocket.events) lists only the hand-seeded reviewed-baseline entry; turn_not_active is not added there because the file is generated and the event extractor is phase-3 - the advisory websocket-events contract tracks this gap for all 25 live events, not just this one.

Browser check covered a streaming turn crossing a real token rotation (held socket, completed turn, deferred reconnect observed in backend logs); an approval-gated coding-workspace turn crossing a rotation was validated at the unit level only.

Shrink pass consolidated the turn-reset duplication into resetTurnState shared with stopGeneration; the parts-vs-content append idiom now exists in three call sites and was deliberately not extracted to keep the diff scoped - noted for a future cleanup.
reason: The frontend's 10-minute access-token refresh rotates the in-memory token, and use-chat's socket-lifecycle effect keys on it, so the live chat WebSocket is torn down and reopened mid-turn; the backend cancels the running turn, releases the sandbox handle, and clears the approval future, after which resume and stop frames on the new socket are silently dropped - the UI shows Running/Waiting-for-approval forever (reproduced 2026-08-25 16:08 UTC, fullstack-app-1 logs). The WS authenticates only at upgrade, so the fix defers the token-swap reconnect until the turn settles, and makes the backend answer no-addressee control frames with an explicit turn_not_active event the frontend reconciles on.
rollback: git revert restores everything; no state outside the repository. In-flight sessions pick the old behaviour up on next page load.
security_impact: None deliberate: no auth logic changed. The WS still authenticates only at upgrade; deferring the reconnect means an open socket keeps operating on the token it authenticated with until the turn settles, which was already the socket's lifetime semantics. turn_not_active carries only frame_type and conversation_id, no token or user data.
summary: Keep in-flight agent turns alive across scheduled token refresh; answer orphaned WS control frames explicitly
